cards.text: Nearly 700 years ago, he wrote about *your* heart.
Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyya. Born in *Damascus,* 1292 CE.
The closest student of *Ibn Taymiyyah,* with him even in prison.
He wrote on the Prophet's way, on patience, on sin and its *cure.*
This series: one book at a *time.*
Something is *worse* than death.
Wasting *time.*
Death cuts you off from this world and its people.
Wasted time cuts you off from *Allah* and the Hereafter.
So what will you do with the next *hour?*
Your heart is a *bird.*
On its journey to Allah, *love* is its head.
Hope and fear are its two *wings.*
Head and wings sound: it flies *well.*
Lose the head, it dies. Lose a wing, it becomes *prey.*
Keep all *three.*
Which heart do *you* have?
The *sound* heart: free of every desire that opposes Allah's command.
The *dead* heart: it doesn't know its Lord, and follows its desires.
The *sick* heart: it has life, and it has illness.
Whichever wins, it *leans* toward.
The work: move it toward the *first.*
Restless, and can't say *why?*
Ibn al-Qayyim heard his teacher, Ibn Taymiyyah, say:
Dhikr is to the heart what *water* is to a fish.
So what happens to a fish taken *out* of the water?
Get back in the *water.*
Sin doesn't announce what it *takes.*
It takes *knowledge,* a light Allah places in the heart.
It can take *provision.*
It brings a *loneliness* between you and Allah.
Doors close. Affairs become *hard.*
But the book is also about the *cure:* repentance, du'a, returning.
Knowledge or *wealth?*
Ibn al-Qayyim explains the famous answer of *Ali* ibn Abi Talib:
Knowledge guards *you.* You guard wealth.
Wealth shrinks when spent. Knowledge *grows* when shared.
Then he gives over a *hundred* more reasons.
Start with one page *today.*
Patience isn't just *waiting.*
Patience in *obeying* Allah, even when it's heavy.
Patience in holding back from what He *forbids.*
Patience with what He *decrees:* the pain you didn't choose.
Which one is *yours* right now?
Written on a *journey.*
Provision for the Hereafter, from the guidance of the best of *creation.*
How he ﷺ prayed, ate, slept and *travelled.*
How he traded, visited the sick, and treated *illness.*
One habit from his life is a good place to *start.*
